item.title: Watch: Missing cat reunites with owner four days after surviving building collapse
item.description: Isaac, a cat missing for four days after a building collapse in Brooklyn, was finally found alive. His owner, Zariah Coleman, had made an emotional appeal for help in locating her pet. Rescue workers discovered Isaac hiding in a cabinet after hearing faint sounds. The cat is currently receiving veterinary care but is expected to be reunited with his owner soon.

item.title: US loses measles-free status after 26 years as virus spreads across country
item.description: The United States is no longer recognized as free of measles, after witnessing a dramatic surge in cases this year. An independent review highlights that measles transmission has continued without interruption for over a year. Falling vaccination rates are identified as a key factor in the disease's resurgence. Experts are urgently calling for a comprehensive strategy to mitigate the outbreak, acknowledging that reinstating measles-elimination status could take several years.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: UK man wins Argos laptop refund battle after court rules activating Windows 11 does not cancel rights
item.description: A landmark court decision has established that buyers can return items purchased online within 14 days of receiving them. A University of Leicester professor successfully challenged retail titan Argos over the return of a laptop. The Court of Appeal ruled that activating pre-installed software does not forfeit the right to a refund. This ruling enhances consumer protection for electronics in the UK, prompting retailers to rethink their return policies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indiana court rejects woman's claim to land after neighbours shift boundary fence
item.description: A legal tussle erupted over a narrow patch of grass between two Indiana neighbors, culminating in a ruling by the Indiana Court of Appeals. They upheld a previous decision in favor of the Goldfarbs, the neighboring property owners. Deanne Ellen Gloppen, attempting to claim ownership via adverse possession, fell short of proving her tax payments included the contested area.

item.title: Married Kentucky teacher breaks down as she admits to sex with 16-year-old student, sharing nude photos
item.description: A married Kentucky teacher and assistant soccer coach, Mary “Hanna” Mattingly, 32, broke down in court as she pleaded guilty to having sexual contact with a 16-year-old student and possessing nude images of him. The former substitute teacher is expected to receive a five-year prison sentence and must register as a sex offender after release.

item.title: Brandi Carlile's charity surpasses $10m in grants, earning 2026 award recognition for its impact
item.description: At the 2026 Anthem Awards, Brandi Carlile shines as the Entertainer of the Year, celebrating a remarkable achievement for her Looking Out Foundation, which recently surpassed $10 million in grants to diverse charitable organizations. With a focus on uplifting LGBTQIA2S+ communities, the foundation inspires fans to donate small amounts, emphasizing that even an average contribution of $25 can create significant change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oprah joins Australian charity drive, packing care bag as campaign targets 150,000 donations
item.description: Oprah Winfrey is lending her support to Share the Dignity’s charity initiative by assembling care bags for women in need. This campaign, which runs from November 6 to November 22, 2026, across Australia, aims to gather 150,000 bags filled with essential items and uplifting notes. These care bags will benefit women struggling with homelessness or domestic violence. Donations are accepted at various Bunnings stores or online throughout the campaign duration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US stalker ordered to pay $18.6 million after stealing woman's Verizon records with fake warrant
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a federal judge in North Carolina has ordered convicted stalker Robert Michael Glauner to pay $18.632 million to a victim for the emotional trauma inflicted upon her. This judgment, which includes punitive damages, stems from Glauner's harassment after he unlawfully procured her private information with a forged search warrant. He was apprehended while attempting to confront her and remains incarcerated.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: El Niño warning: 16 US States at increased risk of flooding this winter
item.description: Meteorologists warn that a robust El Niño, expected to possibly persist until early 2027, will bring about significant weather variations across the country. Warmer northern climates will contrast sharply with increased precipitation in the south, especially affecting the southeastern states and California. Meanwhile, the Pacific Northwest may brace for drier, milder conditions, raising concerns about dwindling water supplies and elevated wildfire risks.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Vance says US will not fight 'forever war' with Iran, defends Trump's military action
item.description: JD Vance emphasized that President Trump will prevent the Iran conflict from becoming a prolonged military commitment. He stated that the administration will avoid a two-year involvement despite external pressures for continued engagement. Vance defended the targeting of Iran’s nuclear program, citing it as a national threat. As tensions remain high, a third US aircraft carrier has been deployed to the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Michigan arts center has reopened its four-level science and history museum after a three-year overhaul, marking a milestone in a $53.2 million renovation; another $1.6 million is still needed for the full project
item.description: The Hall of Ideas at the newly renovated Midland Center of the Arts has reopened following extensive renovations after a 2020 flood. This innovative museum emphasizes interactive learning experiences that blend art, science, and history. With a remarkable $53.2 million renovation project set to conclude by 2027, the centre invites visitors of all ages to explore creative, hands-on exhibits designed to spark imagination and discovery.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Florida conservation groups have permanently protected 22,461 acres of working forests and wetlands in the Apalachicola River Basin, completing the first phase of a larger 41,619-acre project planned for 2030
item.description: In Florida's Apalachicola River Basin, conservation groups have embarked on an ambitious project to protect wetlands and working forests across five counties by the year 2030. This initiative incorporates conservation easements that empower sustainable land use while preserving crucial ecological resources. The area, rich in biodiversity, plays a significant role in supporting local wildlife and economies, ensuring that vital natural assets are sustained for generations to come.

item.title: Former Pakistan army officer is new BLA chief
item.description: Rehman Gul has recently been appointed as the new commander-in-chief of the Baloch Liberation Army. His previous military experience in the Pakistan army adds significant context to his new role. Gul deserted the army in 2010 due to concerns over civilian atrocities, joining the BLA afterward. His appointment follows the resignation of Bashir Zeb from the leadership position amidst various rumors.

item.title: Jeffrey Epstein did not commit suicide, was likely killed: Top forensic expert
item.description: Dr Michael Freeman’s examination of Epstein’s autopsy file raises questions about the nature of his death, suggesting that the injuries sustained are indicative of homicide rather than suicide. He points to signs of a struggle and possible strangulation. In contrast, the New York City medical examiner’s office stands firm on its suicide ruling, but Freeman’s assertions have reignited public interest in conspiracy theories surrounding Epstein’s untimely demise.
